task: Add rate limiting to the public API and prove it holds under load without breaking existing endpoints
loop_altitude_rationale: Multi-module change (middleware + load harness) touching a public surface, but reversible and single-agent — sequential gated stages, no parallel fan-out needed.

selection_log.why: runnable checks exist (contract suite, ratelimit test, load harness exit code) — done is machine-decidable
captured baseline is handed characterize->implement; a green 429 middleware is handed implement->load_verify; each seam is a stable checkable artifact
characterize searches the existing contract; implement is risky middleware needing mid-flight correction; load_verify is a retryable assertion
reversible dev-only change, checks discriminate well — human reviews at gates, not each iteration
stages are strictly sequential (each depends on the prior); no independent fan-out work

per-stage caps; implement_rate_limit restarts its own stalled work (its failures accuse its own middleware, not characterize's baseline — loops-model §V); load_verify loops back to implement; fixer signatures, a blocked task and any public-API change escalate
the contract/ratelimit checks are fast and cheap (npm test in seconds), so frequent small passes (implement cap 8) beat few long ones — tuned: higher caps, retry acceptable on the load stage

digit sweep: iteration caps 4/3/8/5, the stall/zero-change/redesign/restart-budget counters and the fixer-signature counters = decision (pre-registered willingness; the derived entry's sample floor and drift threshold are decision numbers too, tagged inline); the 200-vs-429 threshold boundary and the rps-200 load bar = definitional (red-fixture-backed); the implement-iteration wall-clock budget = empirical, unknowable at 0 runs -> declared derived, measured by characterize

fixed.name: iteration_caps
fixed.why: willingness to spend, pre-registered before the run — a loop may trip a cap, never raise one; changed only outside the loop by the operator (re-examine per design)

fixed.name: stall_and_zero_change_counters
fixed.value_or_location: implement_rate_limit stop_conditions.failure: '2 consecutive iterations fail in the same class' (-> on_failure restart); outer stop_conditions.failure: '2 restarts of one stage without going green', '2 consecutive zero-change iterations', 'redesign forced twice'; load_verify: '3 load retries'
fixed.why: pre-registered routing triggers (D5): in-flight they lose to optimism every time; changed only outside the loop between runs (re-examine per design)

fixed.name: fixer_signature_counters
fixed.value_or_location: stop_conditions.escalate[0]: 'P0/P1 inside the previous iteration's own fix', 'files/tests the fixes touched grew >50% over the last green baseline', 'a third exception layer', 'a second implementation copy', '2 fix rounds on the same defect class'
fixed.why: stop authority, not a world-claim: any one alone stops the loop for the owner's plane question (loops-model.md §V); pre-registered, changed only outside the loop (re-examine per design)

fixed.name: ratelimit_threshold_boundary
fixed.value_or_location: contract A2: HTTP 200 at/below the configured threshold, 429 strictly past it (the 101st request in the example window)
fixed.why: defines what a correct limiter MEANS — loosening it would let an always-429 middleware pass a naive 'a 429 appeared' test
fixed.red_fixture: npm test api:ratelimit -- -t threshold-boundary (goes red on the always-429 implementation)

fixed.name: load_acceptance_bar
fixed.value_or_location: load_verify check + contract A5: p99 under budget with zero 5xx at rps 200, harness must prove achieved rps >= target
fixed.why: defines what 'holds under load' MEANS for this task — loosening the rps target or dropping the achieved-rps assert would let a connection-capped green pass
fixed.red_fixture: node scripts/loadtest.mjs --rps 200 --assert (exits non-zero when the target rps is never reached — the passing-but-wrong ruled out in load_verify)

derived.name: implement_iteration_wallclock_budget
derived.formula: 2 x measured wall-clock of (npm test api:contract && npm test api:ratelimit) on the untouched baseline — one implement iteration = one edit pass + one full check run
derived.cadence: re-derived every time characterize runs (first entry and each loopback into it); never re-derived mid-stage, never by in-flight judgment
derived.sample_rule: >=2 timed suite runs on the untouched baseline (a minimum sample floor: class decision — re-examine per design; it is not a claim about variance); a timed-out run enters as a censored LOWER BOUND, never dropped — a sample that silently drops non-completers is invalid

drift_policy.threshold: inter-derivation drift >50% -> mark unstable and fall back conservative (the 50% is class decision — re-examine per design; the skill recommends no default)
drift_policy.conservative_direction: shrink — the budget is a spend ceiling, so optimism (growing it mid-run) is the failure direction; growth happens only via the formula at the next calibration
drift_policy.floor_trip: if the shrunken budget < the measured cost of ONE full check run, a single honest gate attempt can no longer complete — the minimum-progress floor ('all three stage gates reached and attempted with a real diff') becomes unattainable -> escalate once at contract level, never keep ratcheting

definition_of_done.goal: the existing public-endpoint contract suite passes and is captured as the regression set the later stages must keep green, and every derived parameter is measured into the values artifact (.loop/adaptive-params.json) with its full derivation trail

feedback_signal.falsifiable_when: any existing endpoint returns a different status/body than the captured baseline — the suite goes red; or any managed value in .loop/adaptive-params.json is hand-filled (missing value/derived_from/measured_at/sample_n) — the params check exits non-zero
feedback_signal.passing_but_wrong: a stale/empty contract suite that vacuously passes with zero assertions — ruled out: the suite asserts a concrete status+body per endpoint and fails if the captured baseline file is empty; and a values artifact copied from an old run — ruled out: check_adaptive_params was itself proven against a hand-filled red fixture (a check never seen red on a hand-filled artifact is anti_pattern.unexercised_self_check)

failure: contract suite cannot be made green on the untouched baseline (environment broken, not our change)

definition_of_done.goal: rate-limit middleware returns HTTP 429 past the configured threshold and the contract regression set still passes

feedback_signal.check: npm test api:ratelimit && npm test api:contract
feedback_signal.falsifiable_when: the 101st request inside the window still returns 200 (no 429), or any contract test regresses
feedback_signal.passing_but_wrong: middleware returns 429 for EVERY request (even below the threshold), passing a naive 'a 429 appeared' test — ruled out: the ratelimit test asserts 200 below the threshold AND 429 only above it

failure: 2 consecutive iterations fail in the same class (own-work stall counter: discard this stage's work and restart from the contract in a fresh context, do not patch forward)
the contract regression set goes red (behavior change leaked from this stage's own middleware)

definition_of_done.goal: p99 latency stays under budget at the target RPS with zero 5xx, asserted by the load harness exit code

feedback_signal.falsifiable_when: p99 exceeds the budget or any 5xx is observed at the target RPS — the harness exits non-zero
feedback_signal.passing_but_wrong: the harness reports green because it never actually reached the target RPS (connection-capped) — ruled out: the harness asserts achieved RPS >= target before it judges p99/5xx, exiting non-zero otherwise

failure: p99 budget cannot be met without a public-API change

maker_checker.scope: fresh-context reviewer sees only the diff + the per-stage acceptance checks; flags correctness / stated-requirement gaps only, especially any behavior change to existing endpoints. The reviewer and the stage checks run from a read-only checkout at the stage tag; AGENTS.md (every level), AGENTS.override.md, .codex/, execpolicy .rules files, the .loop/prompts/ evaluator prompt and the graded contract.md are hashed at contract time and verified before launch, so the generator cannot plant standing instructions the reviewer would auto-read or delete an assertion it fails; Codex memories live outside the checkout, so the reviewer's independence from them is recorded as L-i incomplete

planner.mandate: turn the goal into the staged spec + the contract; never write middleware or test code

generator.mandate: write the middleware + load harness to satisfy the contract; may NOT weaken a test or grade its own output

evaluator.mandate: a fresh context that never saw the impl or the generator's reasoning; assume the rate limiter is broken and try to prove it — bypass the window, race the counter, regress an existing endpoint

assertions.must: every pre-existing public endpoint returns its captured baseline status + body (no regression)
the (threshold+1)th request inside the window returns HTTP 429, and every request at or below the threshold returns 200
the 429 response carries a Retry-After header with a positive integer seconds value
the limiter is keyed per client, so one client cannot exhaust another client's quota
p99 latency stays under budget with zero 5xx at the target RPS, and the harness first proves it achieved the target RPS
no test assertion is weakened relative to the pre-change baseline over the whole run
assertions.check: human-verify: the evaluator diffs test/ against the baseline tag captured in stage 1 and confirms no assertion was loosened

assertions.must: the diff stays inside the rate-limit middleware, its tests and the load harness: no tracked or untracked file outside them differs from the baseline tag
the captured contract regression suite is unchanged since the baseline tag, so the generator cannot weaken the set the later stages must keep green
assertions.check: git diff --quiet loop/baseline -- test/api/contract/ && test -z "$(git ls-files -o --exclude-standard -- test/api/contract/)"

assertions.must: once the window elapses, a client that was answered 429 is answered 200 again (the limiter resets instead of banning)
a concurrent burst larger than the threshold admits exactly the threshold count and answers 429 to the rest (no counter race)

harness_primitives: git worktree isolation for reversible work
baseline tag loop/baseline, created by characterize before any code change — the fixed reference A6-A8 diff against
external scratch ledger (.loop/run-state.md) holding which stage is done and what's next across context resets
pre-commit hook runs the current stage's check as a deterministic gate

runtime values artifact (.loop/adaptive-params.json): every managed value carries {value, derived_from, measured_at, sample_n} — written by characterize (the calibration stage), validated by characterize's own check, never by the design linter

stop_conditions.success: every stage's check passes in dependency order and contract A7 passes at the final gate, proving the diff stays within the rate-limit middleware + load harness; minimum-progress floor: all three stage gates must have been reached and attempted with a real diff — a stop below that floor is an escalate, not a success
failure: any stage exhausts its max_iterations without passing its check
a downstream stage forces a redesign of an already-accepted upstream stage twice
2 consecutive outer iterations produce zero new changes (zero-change gate: the loop is spinning, stop rather than keep buying iterations)
a stage's restart budget is spent: 2 restarts of one stage without going green (the restart route itself has stalled — terminal; the per-stage restart counter lives on the stage, not here)
escalate: fixer signature (any one alone; counted on fixes already presented as done, not on pre-green retries): a P0/P1 defect lands inside the previous iteration's own fix, or the files/tests the fixes touched grew >50% over the last green baseline, or a third exception layer lands on one threshold/allow-list, or a second implementation copy of one root cause appears, or 2 fix rounds hit the same defect class -> STOP before any further round; the owner first asks whether this judgment is mechanizable at all (re-plane) and only then rules loopback / restart / abort
the task turns out impossible or blocked on something the loop cannot obtain -> stop and report (safe exit; never sealed by a 'don't ask' instruction)
production permission or real traffic is required to verify
the load target only reproduces against prod
the loop proposes to stop before the minimum-progress floor is reached (premature-abandonment gate)

risk_guards.risk: reward hacking / test overfitting (agent weakens the rate-limit test to pass)
risk_guards.mitigation: the load_verify stage's check is independent of the unit tests; the checker diffs test files

risk_guards.risk: error amplification across stages (a wrong characterize baseline poisons later gates)
risk_guards.mitigation: stage gates run in dependency order; a downstream failure that implicates an upstream gate loops back rather than head-banging in place
no production resources; load test runs against an isolated dev target with least-privilege tokens
